question: Someone without a badge is standing near a secure door, carrying boxes. An employee badges in and, out of politeness, holds the door open for them. What security risk does this create?

options.text: None, this is completely normal and safe
A potential tailgating attack — the visitor gains building access without ever using a badge
The employee has broken the law
The badge reader automatically logs it as two separate valid entries

explanation: Holding a door for someone carrying things is basic politeness, not carelessness — but it means a second person can enter without ever being checked or badging in themselves.

question: Why does a standard badge system fail to catch a tailgating attempt?

options.text: Badge systems are specifically designed to catch this
It only records one valid entry — there's no log at all of the second, unauthorized person
It requires two people to badge in together
It automatically alerts security whenever a door is held open

explanation: The badge reader recorded exactly one valid entry — there's nothing in the system showing that a second, unbadged person also walked in behind them.

question: Why do people rarely challenge a stranger walking confidently through an office?

options.text: Company policy generally forbids questioning anyone
People who look like they belong are rarely challenged, especially in offices too large to know every coworker by sight
It's illegal to question a visitor in most places
Confident-looking visitors are always pre-approved

explanation: Carrying a clipboard and walking with purpose is often enough — most people don't want to be the one who wrongly accuses a coworker they simply don't recognize yet.

question: What's an appropriate way to handle someone in the building without a visible badge?

options.text: Ignore it, it's not your responsibility
Politely ask them to use their own badge or direct them to reception — this is normal, not rude
Immediately call the police
Physically block their path until they explain themselves

explanation: It's okay to politely ask someone without a badge to use their own, or point them to reception — this is a completely normal, non-confrontational thing to do.

question: Why does this simulation matter even though every other one on the platform covers digital attacks?

options.text: It doesn't really matter — physical security is a separate, unrelated concern
Physical access to a device is often the fastest way past every other digital protection in place
It's only relevant to very large companies with big offices
Modern offices no longer have this risk at all

explanation: An unlocked, unattended workstation makes every other security measure irrelevant — once someone is physically at the machine, most digital protections are already bypassed.
